title: Publishing deals and more
notes: Publishing deals, on top of record deals: like Scarlett and Gunnar, a publisher can sign you as a staff writer. You get an advance against your songwriting royalties and a yearly song quota, and they book co-writes, put your songs on hold for stars and review you every year. Find them under Music → Write or Record deal and money.
The writing room: a 3D co-write where you and your co-writer trade lines, then you arrange the song yourself (verse, chorus, bridge) and the structure is rated.
Producer arguments in the studio, raw demos that can become cult hits, and session guitar work.
Work the crowd: duets with a friend (wait for their verse, nail the harmonies), on-stage mishaps (broken strings, dead in-ears, rain) and fans shouting for requests.
The Bluebird is now its own 3D room. Opening for a star means winning over a half-empty arena.
International tours to the UK and Ireland, Canada and Australia, music video shoots with a 3D cutscene, and late-night TV appearances.
Episode titles now come from what happened that week, plus season trailers, cold opens, to-camera confessionals and fan theories about your songs.
Group chats (the Exes, family, Highway 65, your band), family dinners, and characters who age and change over the seasons.
A career timeline with charts and stats, challenge runs (broke and scared, no label ever, one year to make it), and music that sounds like your genre.
